This digest covers a 30-day window from 2026-01-17 to 2026-02-16 and represents a 30% subsample (subsample_frac: 0.3, RNG seed: 102) of the underlying USGS-synthetic catalog; true event counts and regional frequencies for the full catalog are approximately 3.3× higher than figures reported here.
the digest contains no depth-of-burial uncertainty values, no magnitude uncertainty ranges, and no station-coverage metadata, limiting confidence in precise depth and magnitude characterizations
indicating sustained seismic loading in this area
criticisms: 'indicating sustained seismic loading in this area' is a mechanistic interpretation that goes somewhat beyond what frequency counts alone can establish — the data shows clustering but does not directly measure stress loading; hedged language like 'may suggest' would be more appropriate.

The claim that true event counts are 'approximately 3.3× higher' is a reasonable inference from the 30% subsample fraction, but the report states this with more confidence than warranted — the subsample may not be uniformly distributed, so the multiplier could be misleading.

The Risk Watch section frames Tobelo as warranting 'priority monitoring' and Kermadec as needing 'continuous tsunami-alert watch' without explicitly noting that these recommendations are based on a partial (30%) dataset, which is only acknowledged later in the Data Caveats section — the sequencing creates a risk that readers act on the recommendations before encountering the caveat.
